answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents join via cryptographic attestation chains verified by zero-knowledge proofs. Each new identity requires a staked deposit evaluated against historical network growth; any marginal delta in registration rate triggers exponential capital exhaustion, making Sybil swarms financially unviable. Like trees rooted across an orchard or surveyor beacons atop an open knoll, genuine agents establish persistent, verifiable trust anchors.
